intended_object: A Coxeter system: a group W together with a family of generators (s_i)_{i∈B} for which W has the Coxeter presentation ⟨s_i | (s_i s_j)^{m_ij}⟩ given by a Coxeter matrix M. Here it is recorded as an isomorphism W ≃ M.Group (from the docstring and the module).
explanation: `M.Group` is `PresentedGroup M.relationsSet`, the group with generators indexed by B and relations (s_i s_{i'})^{M i i'}. The Coxeter matrix is symmetric, has 1s on the diagonal and entries ≠ 1 off the diagonal. An entry of 0 encodes m = ∞, because x^0 = 1 is a trivial relation. A group isomorphism W ≃* M.Group is the same data as a generating family s_i := mulEquiv⁻¹(simple i) in W for which W has the Coxeter presentation. So this is exactly a Coxeter system (W, S), with S indexed by B and the matrix fixed. The index type B is arbitrary and W is any group, so the generality is the natural one. This is Mathlib's own standard definition of the notion.
